connector: Welcome to a new book. I mend old books for a living, and this one I’ve read every winter since I was nine. Four children are sitting at a train station when something pulls at them. Where do they land, and when? Read for clues the way you’d read the cracks in an old binding: each one tells you how much time has passed.

a.why: Capital A starts the sentence; commas separate the four things in the list, including the one before and; a period ends it.

b.why: Capital T starts the sentence; commas separate the four things the children found, including the one before and; a period ends it.

notes.wgrd: In a fantasy setting, collect place clues (what the children see and touch) and time clues (what has crumbled or grown wild). Then say where and when they are in one sentence.
vocab: A place where things meet or connect, especially where train lines split.
A dense group of bushes or small trees growing closely together.
Thorny bushes, especially wild blackberry or raspberry bushes with prickly stems.
Lived in; having people or creatures living there.
notes.wordParts: Prefixes: pre- = before, re- = again or back, trans- = across, inter- = between: preview, return, transport, international.
notes.grammar: Conjunctions join ideas. And adds one idea to another; or offers a choice between them. Stay in the castle or ride into the woods means one, not both.
notes.spelling: To split a long word, peel off the prefix and suffix first, then the base is easy: un + familiar, transport + ed, discover + ed.

why.t: In Chapter 2, the children find the treasure chamber of their old castle, dusty and forgotten, its treasures waiting in the dark. Each word you build sets one treasure back in its place. This week’s word parts tell when and where: pre- (before), re- (again), trans- (across) and inter- (between).

wordgame.win: Four treasures are back in their niches. pre- = before, re- = again, trans- = across, inter- = between.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: The OAO Seven Pillars are honesty, respect, courtesy, responsibility, courage, service and perseverance. In Chapter 1 the children are hungry, thirsty and lost. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: There are only two lunches among four children. They divide the sandwiches into four portions, even though nobody has quite enough.
items.why: They share fairly with each other instead of each keeping their own.
items.hint: Think about who gets the food.

items.t: Edmund and Lucy want to leave their shoes on the beach. Susan says they might never find them again, and they will want them when night comes and it gets cold.
items.why: Susan thinks ahead about what the group will need later.

items.t: Peter thinks they may soon have to eat eggs raw, but he doesn’t say it out loud. Then he says, “Come on, Ed is right. And we must try to do something.”
items.why: He keeps the others from losing heart and keeps the group moving.
items.hint: What does Peter do instead of complaining?

morphology.label: Nell · prefixes of time and place

transcripts.welcome: Hello, I’m Nell. I mend old books, and this one I’ve read every winter since I was nine. It’s called Prince Caspian. Four children are waiting at a train station, and then they aren’t. Today’s question: what kind of place have they arrived at, and what clues tell you?
transcripts.read: Read like a detective with a magnifying glass. Every time Lewis names something the children can see or touch, picture it. The water, the trees, the stone. Then watch for things that have crumbled or gone wild. Those tell you how long a place has been left alone.
transcripts.morphology: Some word parts tell you when and where. Pre means before. Re means again, or back. Trans means across. Inter means between. Find the part at the front, ask what it adds to the word, and set one more treasure back in its place.
